name: Earth and environment: WeatherBench probabilistic forecast calibration
description: Calibrate fixed operational ensemble forecasts using prior-year history and evaluate their predictive distributions against independently aligned future-year reanalysis.

sources.locator: WeatherBench2 forecast evaluation, probabilistic ensembleCRPS, ERA5 reference data and area weighting.
Official source data/evaluation reference; evaluator and seed independently written.

sources.title: Calibrated Probabilistic Forecasting Using Ensemble Model Output Statistics and Minimum CRPS Estimation
sources.locator: Develops ensemble forecast postprocessing that corrects bias and dispersion using historical observations and CRPS. The local WeatherBench2 IFS/ERA5 chronological subset is a separate application of this calibration task.

requirements.datasets: SHA256-locked source bundle E03.json in .cache/science-earth-data. Automatically prepared by scripts/prepare_earth_data.py.

evaluation.benchmark: Earth and environment: WeatherBench probabilistic forecast calibration
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: calibrate(forecast,lead_hours,locations,training_history) -> finite n x1..128 ensemble. Fixed WeatherBench forecasts and ERA5 target, lat/lon locations and prior-year labeled training history. Exact empirical-ensemble CRPS, latitude weights, training-only extreme threshold and Brier diagnostic. No evaluation labels provided.

provenance.note: Local evaluator, candidate interface and seed recreated from scientific specifications; official benchmark data are reused.

limitations: IFS50-member2m-temperature24-hour forecasts on64×32 grid: monthly2018 training versus monthly2019 evaluation at64 locations. ERA5 is reanalysis, not independent raw weather observation. TIGGE data have research-use restrictions; this is a small chronological adaptation.
Source data remain local caches with immutable revisions/content hashes and no evaluator network access. Public subsets are development-visible; freeze candidates before wider generalization tests.
Improved source benchmark performance is a scientific-method contribution, not alone a new discovery or operational forecast validation.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Produce reliable probabilistic weather forecasts by correcting ensemble bias and spread.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Calibrated forecast uncertainty helps users reason about weather-dependent outcomes.

papers.title: Calibrated Probabilistic Forecasting Using Ensemble Model Output Statistics and Minimum CRPS Estimation
papers.primary_goal: Correct bias and underdispersion in weather ensembles to improve predictive distributions.
papers.task_relation: The local IFS 2 m temperature task applies this forecast-calibration problem to a historical prior-year/future-year split with ERA5 verification. The paper does not validate the local alignment, reanalysis truth assumption or operational skill.
